title: Tissue Freezing for seqFISH
author: Nina Dar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7mdhk26
materials: Tissue fixation and freezing in OCT

steps.title: Prepare Freezing Containers
steps.instruction: Set up the cooling environments for sample freezing and storage.

substeps.instruction: Place dry ice in a cold-proof container and pour 100% EtOH over the ice.
Prepare a separate closed container with dry ice for samples that have already been frozen.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Labeling
steps.instruction: Create identification labels for the samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare stickers with identifying details on the sample.
Attach the stickers to a piece of foil.

steps.title: Prepare Embedding Mold
steps.instruction: Clean tools and prepare the mold for the sample.

steps.title: Embed Sample in OCT
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample into the mold and encapsulate it.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the sample using tweezers or, for small samples, a glass pipette with a broken thin edge to prevent the sample from sticking.
Place the sample in the mold and cover with OCT until the mold is completely full.

steps.title: Freeze the Sample
steps.instruction: Carefully freeze the embedded sample using the EtOH/dry ice bath.

substeps.instruction: Using tweezers, gently place the mold into the EtOH.
Hold the mold with tweezers until it is completely frozen, ensuring only the bottom side of the mold touches the EtOH; do not dump the mold into the liquid.

steps.title: Store Frozen Samples
steps.instruction: Maintain the frozen state of the samples before long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Allow the frozen sample to float on the EtOH until all samples are processed, or move it to the closed container with dry ice.
Cover the frozen samples with foil and transfer them on ice or in the dry ice container to -80°C.
